title: Changes of Active Substances and Antioxidant Activity as Well as Microbial Diversity and Community Structure During the Natural Fermentation of Dendrobium Jiaosu
content: Dendrobium officinale has long been valued for its medicinal properties. This study investigated the alterations in bioactive compounds, antioxidant activity, and microbial communities during the 50-day natural fermentation process of Dendrobium jiaosu. The antioxidant activity fluctuated, reaching its peak around days 20-25. The total antioxidant capacity and superoxide dismutase activity showed a positive correlation, reaching peak levels around day 10. The correlation analysis showed positive relationships between antioxidant capacity and flavonoids, sugars, and phenols. An analysis of 16S rRNA sequencing revealed that unclassified Enterobacteriaceae and Sporolactobacillus were the main taxa in the initial stages, but were subsequently replaced by a diverse range of genera. The correlation analysis showed a positive relationship between Klebsiella and antioxidant markers. Phenylbacterium showed a positive correlation, while Weissella and Sporolactobacillus exhibited a negative correlation with 2,2′-Azinobis- (3-ethylbenzthiazoline-6-sulphonate) (ABTS) scavenging. Chitinophaga exhibited an inverse correlation with amino acids. An analysis of the metabolic pathway showed heightened activity in carbohydrate, amino acid, and lipid metabolism in the later stage. Significant changes in phytochemicals, antioxidants, and microbiota were observed during extended fermentation. The findings offer valuable insights for improving fermentation processes to enhance the quality and functionality of Dendrobium jiaosu.
